title: Docker build fails at npm install
problem: Docker image build fails during npm install.
likely_cause: Invalid package configuration, dependency conflicts, or network issues.
fix_steps: Read the complete npm error.
Check package.json and package-lock.json.
Run npm ci locally to verify dependencies.
Rebuild the image after correcting the issue.
extra_tips: Use a consistent Node.js version.
Avoid copying unnecessary files into the build context.

title: Docker container exits immediately
problem: A Docker container starts and then stops.
likely_cause: The main process exits, the application crashes, or its startup command is incorrect.
fix_steps: Check docker logs <container>.
Inspect the container exit code.
Verify the Dockerfile CMD or ENTRYPOINT.
Correct the application error and restart the container.
extra_tips: Containers stay alive only while their main process runs.

title: Docker port conflict
problem: Docker cannot bind an application to a host port.
likely_cause: Another process or container is already using the port.
fix_steps: Check which process uses the port.
Inspect running containers and port mappings.
Stop or reconfigure the conflicting service if appropriate.
Restart the container with an available port.
extra_tips: Do not stop unfamiliar production services without approval.

title: Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff
problem: A Kubernetes container repeatedly crashes and restarts.
likely_cause: Application errors, incorrect configuration, failed probes, or insufficient resources.
fix_steps: Run kubectl describe pod <pod-name>.
Check kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous.
Review configuration, probes, and resource limits.
Apply a verified fix and monitor the pod.
extra_tips: Previous container logs often reveal the original crash.

title: Kubernetes ImagePullBackOff
problem: Kubernetes cannot pull a container image.
likely_cause: Wrong image name or tag, missing registry access, or invalid image pull credentials.
fix_steps: Run kubectl describe pod <pod-name>.
Verify the image name and tag.
Check registry availability and permissions.
Verify imagePullSecrets if the registry is private.
extra_tips: Avoid putting registry passwords directly in manifests.

title: AWS S3 AccessDenied
problem: An AWS S3 operation returns AccessDenied.
likely_cause: Missing IAM permissions, bucket policy restrictions, or an explicit deny.
fix_steps: Identify the IAM principal making the request.
Review IAM and bucket policies.
Check the required S3 action and resource ARN.
Retry only after an authorized policy correction.
extra_tips: Grant only the permissions required for the task.

title: AWS EC2 connection timeout
problem: A connection to an EC2 instance times out.
likely_cause: Security group rules, routing, network ACLs, or instance availability problems.
fix_steps: Confirm the instance is running.
Check the public or private network path.
Review security groups and network ACLs.
Verify that SSH or the required service is listening.
extra_tips: Allow access only from trusted networks.

title: GitHub Actions workflow fails
problem: A GitHub Actions workflow fails during a job.
likely_cause: A failing command, missing secret, incorrect workflow configuration, or environment mismatch.
fix_steps: Open the failed workflow run.
Inspect the first meaningful error in the logs.
Check YAML syntax, versions, and required secrets.
Correct the cause and rerun the workflow.
extra_tips: Never print secrets in workflow logs.

title: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway
problem: A gateway or proxy returns HTTP 502.
likely_cause: The upstream server is unavailable, unreachable, or returning an invalid response.
fix_steps: Check the upstream application's health.
Inspect reverse proxy and application logs.
Verify upstream host, port, and protocol.
Test connectivity between the proxy and upstream service.
extra_tips: Check whether the issue started after a deployment.

title: Application out of memory
problem: An application crashes or is terminated because memory is exhausted.
likely_cause: Memory leaks, excessive workload, or insufficient configured memory.
fix_steps: Inspect application and system memory metrics.
Check container termination reason and memory limits.
Look for leaks or unusually large workloads.
Tune resource limits only after reviewing capacity.
extra_tips: Increasing memory alone may hide an underlying leak.

title: Docker image not found
problem: Docker cannot find or pull the requested image.
likely_cause: Incorrect image name or tag, missing image, or private registry access restrictions.
fix_steps: Verify the image repository and tag.
Check whether the image exists in the registry.
Authenticate to the registry if required.
Confirm access permissions and retry.
extra_tips: Use explicit version tags instead of relying on latest.

title: Docker permission denied
problem: A user cannot access the Docker daemon or a mounted file.
likely_cause: Insufficient operating-system permissions or incorrect file ownership.
fix_steps: Read the complete permission error.
Check Docker daemon status and socket permissions.
Review ownership and access to mounted files.
Apply the approved least-privilege permission change.
extra_tips: Do not change permissions broadly or expose the Docker socket unnecessarily.

title: Docker container cannot resolve DNS
problem: A container cannot resolve a hostname.
likely_cause: DNS configuration problems, network isolation, or an incorrect hostname.
fix_steps: Verify the hostname and DNS record.
Test name resolution inside the container.
Inspect Docker network configuration.
Check the host's DNS and network connectivity.
extra_tips: Containers on the same custom network can resolve one another by service or container name.

title: Docker volume data missing
problem: Application data is missing after a container restart or recreation.
likely_cause: Data was stored in the container's writable layer or the wrong volume path was mounted.
fix_steps: Inspect the container's mount configuration.
Check the source volume or host directory.
Verify the application's data path.
Restore from backup if data was lost.
extra_tips: Use persistent volumes for important data and test backups.

title: Kubernetes pod stuck Pending
problem: A Kubernetes pod remains in Pending state.
likely_cause: Insufficient cluster resources, scheduling constraints, or unavailable persistent volumes.
fix_steps: Run kubectl describe pod <pod-name>.
Read scheduling events.
Check node capacity, selectors, taints, and tolerations.
Review persistent volume claims if applicable.
extra_tips: Use the scheduler event message to identify the specific blocker.

title: Kubernetes Service unreachable
problem: An application cannot reach a Kubernetes Service.
likely_cause: Incorrect selectors, missing endpoints, wrong service port, or network policy restrictions.
fix_steps: Inspect the Service and its selectors.
Check whether ready pod endpoints exist.
Verify port and targetPort values.
Review network policies and application listening ports.
extra_tips: A Service can exist even when it has no usable endpoints.

title: Kubernetes pod ImagePullSecret failure
problem: A pod cannot authenticate to a private image registry.
likely_cause: Missing, invalid, or incorrectly scoped registry credentials.
fix_steps: Check pod events for authentication errors.
Confirm the Secret exists in the pod's namespace.
Verify the Secret type and registry address.
Refresh credentials using an approved secure process.
extra_tips: Do not paste registry credentials into chat or source control.

title: Kubernetes liveness probe failing
problem: Kubernetes repeatedly restarts a container after liveness probe failures.
likely_cause: Incorrect probe path or port, slow startup, or an unhealthy application.
fix_steps: Inspect pod events and probe configuration.
Verify the configured path and port.
Check application startup time and health.
Adjust probe timing only when justified by observed behavior.
extra_tips: Use a startup probe for applications that need longer to initialize.

title: Kubernetes ConfigMap or Secret missing
problem: A pod cannot start because a referenced ConfigMap or Secret is unavailable.
likely_cause: The resource is missing, incorrectly named, or in another namespace.
fix_steps: Inspect pod events.
Verify the resource name and namespace.
Check the pod's environment or volume references.
Create or correct the resource through the approved deployment process.
extra_tips: Keep credentials in Kubernetes Secrets or an approved secret manager.

title: AWS IAM role credentials unavailable
problem: An AWS SDK or CLI cannot obtain credentials.
likely_cause: Missing credential configuration, an unavailable instance role, or an incorrect execution environment.
fix_steps: Identify where the application runs.
Check the configured AWS credential provider.
Verify that the intended role is attached and available.
Check relevant SDK or CLI error messages.
extra_tips: Prefer temporary role credentials over hardcoded access keys.

title: AWS EC2 instance status check failed
problem: An EC2 instance fails a status check.
likely_cause: Underlying host issues, operating-system problems, or incorrect network configuration.
fix_steps: Check instance and system status checks in AWS.
Review the system log and console output.
Inspect recent configuration changes.
Follow AWS recovery guidance appropriate to the failed check.
extra_tips: Preserve important data before attempting recovery actions.

title: AWS S3 bucket access or region error
problem: An S3 request fails because the endpoint or bucket region is incorrect.
likely_cause: The client is using an endpoint or region that does not match the bucket.
fix_steps: Confirm the bucket's actual region.
Check the region configured in the SDK or CLI.
Use the appropriate regional endpoint.
Retry and inspect any remaining error.
extra_tips: Do not assume a bucket's region from the application's region.

title: CI/CD pipeline test stage fails
problem: A CI/CD pipeline fails during automated tests.
likely_cause: A real regression, missing test dependency, environment difference, or flaky test.
fix_steps: Open the failing test logs.
Identify the first failed assertion or setup step.
Reproduce the test in a matching environment.
Fix the underlying cause and rerun the relevant tests.
extra_tips: Do not skip failing tests just to make a pipeline green.

title: CI/CD deployment fails due to missing environment variable
problem: An application fails to start or deploy because a required environment variable is absent.
likely_cause: The variable was not configured in the deployment environment or its name differs from the application configuration.
fix_steps: Read the startup error.
List required variable names without exposing their values.
Check environment-specific configuration.
Add missing values through the approved secret or configuration manager.
extra_tips: Never print secret values in pipeline logs.

title: CI/CD pipeline permission denied
problem: A workflow cannot access a repository resource or perform an action.
likely_cause: Insufficient token permissions, repository policy restrictions, or an unauthorized deployment identity.
fix_steps: Identify the operation that was denied.
Review workflow and repository permissions.
Grant only the required permissions.
Rerun the workflow and verify the result.
extra_tips: Use least-privilege token permissions.

title: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
problem: A server returns HTTP 503 because it cannot currently handle the request.
likely_cause: Overload, maintenance, unhealthy upstream services, or insufficient available capacity.
fix_steps: Check service health and monitoring metrics.
Inspect application and proxy logs.
Verify dependency and upstream availability.
Restore capacity or service health and monitor recovery.
extra_tips: Use retries with backoff where appropriate; avoid retry storms.

title: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout
problem: A gateway returns HTTP 504 because an upstream response took too long.
likely_cause: A slow application, overloaded dependency, network delay, or overly restrictive timeout.
fix_steps: Inspect gateway and application logs.
Measure upstream response time.
Check database and external service latency.
Fix the slow dependency before changing timeouts.
extra_tips: Increasing timeouts alone may hide performance problems.

title: Application connection refused
problem: A client receives a connection refused error when contacting a service.
likely_cause: No service is listening on the destination port, or the host or port is incorrect.
fix_steps: Verify the destination hostname and port.
Check whether the service is running and listening.
Inspect container or host port mappings.
Review firewall and network configuration.
extra_tips: Inside a container, localhost refers to that container itself.

title: Git merge conflict in deployment branch
problem: Git cannot automatically merge conflicting changes.
likely_cause: Different branches changed overlapping lines or files.
fix_steps: Run git status to identify conflicted files.
Review both changes and edit the conflict markers.
Run relevant tests after resolving conflicts.
Stage resolved files and complete the merge or rebase.
extra_tips: Do not discard another contributor's changes without reviewing them.

title: TLS or SSL certificate error
problem: A client cannot establish a trusted TLS connection.
likely_cause: An expired certificate, hostname mismatch, incomplete certificate chain, or untrusted certificate authority.
fix_steps: Read the complete certificate error.
Verify certificate expiry and hostname.
Check the certificate chain and server configuration.
Renew or correctly configure the certificate using an approved process.
extra_tips: Do not disable certificate verification as a permanent fix.
